reelection.rule: Rule: next even-year November for this House term. legislators-current.yaml ends the current term on 2027-01-03. The even-year November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file has no election day, so no day of the month is shown.

vote_frequency.label: In this cached set only (the latest 40 House roll calls, not a lifetime record): 40 of 40. Yea or Aye: 34. Nay or No: 6. Not Voting: 0. donor_industry.caption: From itemized individual contributions over $200 reported to the FEC, grouped by the donor's self-reported employer and occupation. Last week, President Trump took action to provide harvest-season relief by allowing red-dyed diesel for on-road use, delivering farmers meaningful savings. While Iowa, Illinois, and Nebraska have acted, Governor Tim Walz refuses to follow suit.

Once again, Gov. Walz is putting politics ahead of Minnesota farmers. Read our letter calling for action ⬇️

Big thank you to the team at Sargent’s North Landscape and Garden Center in Rochester for having me on Friday! Serving #MN01 for over 50 years, it was great to get their insights on the local workforce and business climate. https://t.co/k94n2bQahJ

As Rochester continues to grow, we need infrastructure that keeps up with that growth, improves mobility, and supports residents and local businesses. Last week in Rochester, we celebrated the 6th Street Bridge Project’s $19.9 million in federal funding that I helped deliver, which will be used for the design and construction of a bridge to connect neighbors across the Zumbro River.

I’m proud to support projects that will deliver real results for southern Minnesotans, and I’ll continue to advocate for infrastructure improvements throughout #MN01 that make our towns and cities even better places to live for future generations.

Happy National Farmer’s Day! It’s an honor to be one of the very few active farmers in Congress representing my fellow southern Minnesota producers. As a member of @HouseAgGOP and strong supporter of the Working Families Tax Cuts, which delivered the largest investment in the farm safety net since the 2002 Farm Bill, I’ve delivered commonsense, meaningful legislation that empowers the men and women who feed and fuel the world. I’ll continue working with my colleagues in Washington and listening to farmers in Minnesota’s First District to deliver these wins time and time again.

Happy National 4-H Week! Our #MN01 4-H programs give kids the hands-on experience and peer mentorship they need to be tomorrow’s leaders. By building leadership and communication skills that last them a lifetime, these young people are stepping up to improve the world around them. A big thanks to all 4-H members and volunteers for your unwavering dedication to the next generation!

Great to be in Mankato this week to visit the Mankato Regional Airport (MKT) and check out the site of their proposed air traffic control tower – a project I secured $3.5 million for during the FY26 appropriations process. MKT has become the second busiest airport in the state for takeoffs and touchdowns behind MSP, making this a much-needed addition for improved safety.

This week, I had the chance to visit with the team at RISE Modular’s manufacturing facility in Owatonna to hear more about their work and innovative solutions to deliver custom-designed multifamily and hospitality projects, like hotels and apartment buildings, throughout the country. It’s always great to meet with our local manufacturers and home builders here in #MN01 - thanks for having me!

Thank you to everyone in attendance at yesterday’s Rural Water Roundtable in Eagle Lake, especially my friend @RepDustyJohnson, for joining me in #MN01 and hearing from Minnesotans about the importance of strong, reliable water systems in our communities.

In the FY26 appropriations process, I secured $11.4 million in funding for rural water infrastructure projects across southern Minnesota, and I appreciated yesterday’s conversation to hear how these dollars are positively impacting residents across the First District.

Thank you to the brave men and women of @FBIMinneapolis and U.S. Attorney Daniel Rosen for taking swift action to apprehend Sheikhdoon Abdullahi Mohamud, charged with plotting a terrorist attack at the Mall of America.

Because of the coordinated counterterrorism efforts across multiple agencies, this extremist’s plot was foiled, American lives were saved, and this individual will now be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law.

https://t.co/FhjcFwBxYI

Last week, I joined a Q&A session in Trimont, hosted by my friends at @MNFarmBureau. As a fourth-generation farmer and member of @HouseAgGOP, I’ve championed policies to help our #MN01 farmers, like the House-passed Farm Bill, year-round, nationwide E15, and repealing the egregious Prop 12 mandate. I appreciate having these meaningful conversations to hear more about how I can continue to advocate for our ag industry while serving in Washington, D.C.

Avian metapneumovirus (aMPV) has severely impacted Minnesota turkey flocks. Minnesota is the top turkey-producing state in the nation, which is why I led my fellow members of our Minnesota Congressional Delegation in sending a letter to @SecRollins urging the administration to take meaningful steps to address the significant losses our turkey growers have experienced. ⬇️

While in Martin County last week, I was able to get an update from local officials on their plans to renovate the regional public safety and justice center in Fairmont. I was proud to secure $1.1 million in funding for these important updates that will ensure our local law enforcement officers have the proper resources to keep our communities safe.

financial_disclosures.caption: Official House financial disclosure filings from the Clerk of the House. A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. This page links to the Clerk's copies and does not score anyone.

funding.heading: Disclosed campaign receipts
funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.

town_halls.note: There is no national town-hall dataset. Dates are not estimated.

disclosure_note: Disclosed contributions only; donors behind groups that do not report their own donors are not in this feed.
vote_scope: This is not a full career record. The cache is the latest 40 House rolls (2026, rolls 275-314) and 40 Senate votes (119th Congress, session 2, votes 217-256).
